audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated mechanics run through the whole page. (1) K'Sante's Q is repeatedly called a knock-up that 'walls' you — 'Dodge his Q wall-knockups', 'Get walled by his Q', 'his Q can knock you out of a Body Slam', 'Q-knockup chip', 'Q-knockup poke'. (2) early claims 'his percent-HP passive makes his Ntofo autos hurt more the longer you stand in them'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Ntofo Strikes damages and SLOWS in a short line, and at 2 stacks fires a shockwave that PULLS enemies in — there is no knock-up and no wall interaction on Q. The knock-back-and-stun is Path Maker (W); the through-a-wall knockback is All Out (R). Dauntless Instinct, the passive, marks a target to take more damage on his NEXT attack — it is a one-shot mark, not percent-HP ramping damage. Both errors point the player at the wrong ability to dodge, and one of them tells him to fear standing in autos that do not scale that way.
audit.corrected: Q rewritten as a slow that pulls at 2 stacks, W named as the charge-up that both reduces his damage taken and stuns, R named as the wall-knockback. The passive re-described as a damage mark on his next attack. The one genuinely favourable interaction added: when he is All Out, Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns, so his R form loses the CC that beats your engage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts gave K'Sante levels 2, 3 and first item while their own why-text says 'Happy Hour out-heals his poke', 'W max plus Happy Hour wins the extended trades' and 'it's a coin-flip window'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill/Gragas/Skill/Gragas/Skill/Skill/K'Sante, matching the prose: Gragas wins the sustain windows at 2 and 4-5, level 3 and 6 are even, K'Sante takes over at two items with All Out.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group to Skill, Gragas, Skill, Gragas, Skill, Skill, K'Sante.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never names a single K'Sante ability — the packet flags this explicitly — and no cooldown appears anywhere.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is 3.5s, so it is always available and the pull is the thing to count, not dodge once. Path Maker is 14s at rank 1, Footwork 10s, All Out 120s at rank 1. Those numbers define the trade windows.
audit.corrected: Ability names and cooldowns written into the cooldown block, trading rules, do's and don'ts.

edits.before: K'Sante is clunky early too, so the first levels are a sustain race you can win — grab Q+W at 2 and trade with a W-empowered auto plus a detonated cask, then let Happy Hour heal the chip. Don't waste your E dashing in at level 3; his W blocks a chunk of your damage and his Q can knock you up mid-collision, so save the stun for a committed trade. Respect that his percent-HP passive makes his Ntofo autos hurt more the longer you stand in them, so keep trades short and lean on your healing between them.
edits.after: K'Sante is clunky early too, so the first levels are a sustain race you can win — grab Q+W at 2 and trade with a W-empowered auto plus a detonated cask, then let Happy Hour heal the chip. Don't waste your E dashing in at level 3; Path Maker charges up taking reduced damage and then stuns you mid-collision, so save the stun for a committed trade. Count his Ntofo Strikes stacks instead: the second one fires a shockwave that pulls you in and starts his all-in.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your best window — W max and Happy Hour mean you out-sustain his Q-knockup poke in any extended trade, so force the long fights before his first tank item lands. At 6 you get E-W-Q plus Explosive Cask for a genuine all-in, but his R isolates you off your team and pulls you out of the dive, so it isn't a clean kill — use the cask to knock him off you or back toward your tower rather than expecting a solo kill. Trade on your terms, hold E to body-slam away from his Q follow-up, and ping for a gank since his pre-R mobility is just the one W dash.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your best window — W max and Happy Hour mean you out-sustain his 3.5s Ntofo chip in any extended trade, so force the long fights before his first tank item lands. At 6 he gets All Out, which knocks you back THROUGH a wall and then dashes after you, so it isn't a clean kill for you — use the cask to knock him off you or back toward your tower rather than expecting a solo kill. Hold E until Path Maker's 14s is spent, and ping for a gank: pre-6 his only mobility is that one W dash and Footwork on 10s.

notes: Two fabrications corrected across the page: K'Sante's Q was described as a knock-up that walls you (it slows, and pulls at 2 stacks — the knockback-stun is Path Maker, the wall-knockback is All Out), and his passive was described as percent-HP ramping damage (Dauntless Instinct marks a target for extra damage on his next attack). The full layer named none of his abilities at all, which the packet flagged; every full-layer string I touched now names the real ability. Added the one favourable interaction the page never claimed: while All Out, Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns. Charts on both layers flipped as an atomic group to the packet.
